TCFD－Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The primary guiding principle is for the HKMA to prioritise ESG investments where the risk-adjusted long-term returns are comparable to those of other projects, in line with the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives. Details of the HKMA’s responsible investment framework are available on the HKMA website: The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing the ESG and climate-related risks involved in the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors progress in the integration of ESG factors into investments and the Exchange Fund’s ESG profile through regular meeting reports from the Risk Management and Compliance Division of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 1, the ESG Committee established under the Exchange Fund Investment Office is chaired by the Chief Risk Officer and is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the various ESG initiatives of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. The motions discussed and progress of work at each ESG Committee meeting are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Oversight and governance structure for responsible investment The dedicated team in the Risk Management and Compliance Division works closely with the investment teams of the Exchange Fund Investment Office on integrating ESG factors and assists the senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing ESG and climate-related risks and opportunities across various types of investments: Public market investments The Credit, Rules and Compliance Committee, comprising senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, monitors the ESG profile of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Compliance Division. In addition, the Risk Management and Compliance Division participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (see the section “Striving for Active Ownership” under “Risk Management” on page 27 for details). Private market investments The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments of each investment proposal conducted by the Risk Management and Compliance Division and the private market investment teams. Tangible evidence² continues to show that climate change and related risks have a significant impact. According to the latest report3 of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), even assuming that the announced “nationally determined contribution” targets of all regions are fully implemented, the rise in global temperature by 2100 is still estimated to be as high as 2.1 to 2.4 degrees Celsius, making it difficult to achieve the Paris Agreement’s goal of keeping the increase in the global average temperature below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. If regions adopt more aggressive policy measures to narrow the temperature gap, the resulting transition risks⁴ and market repricing of assets based on anticipated future trends, together with inherent physical risks, will intensify pressure on asset valuations. In view of updates to the global warming trajectory and modelling assumptions, the HKMA drew on the expertise of external consultants to further assess the resilience of the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” under the “Rapid Transition” scenario (Figure 2), in addition to the scenarios assessed in 2021. The “Rapid Transition” scenario incorporates higher transition risk factors over the short, medium and long term, assuming that policy changes and technological developments together drive a rapid decline in carbon emissions, while multiple assets are abruptly divested to keep the increase in average temperature within 1.5 degrees Celsius before 2100. This scenario is broadly consistent with the disorderly scenario recommended by the NGFS for forward-looking climate impact assessments. The “Investment Portfolio” remains resilient over the medium to long term because a relatively large proportion of its asset allocation comprises sovereign bonds, which are less sensitive to transition impacts. Sectoral distribution is critical. Low-carbon power and renewable energy assets may benefit from the transition. Transition risks and asset repricing may adversely affect performance in the short term, particularly equity assets. The “Investment Portfolio” as a whole will suffer increasingly severe impacts from physical risks that gradually emerge over time. Energy and traditional utilities remain the most vulnerable sectors. Climate scenarios, like other modelling approaches, have their limitations. The analysis is based on the sector distribution of market benchmarks at the strategic asset allocation level and does not take into account the effects of actively selecting specific securities within a sector. More in-depth research shows that the investments in the “Investment Portfolio” are generally more resilient to transition shocks or suffer less severe impacts than the strategic asset allocation market benchmarks. This result further confirms that the HKMA’s responsible investment approach focusing on combating climate change can enhance portfolio resilience. The climate change trajectory remains uncertain, and scenario analysis methodologies will continue to evolve as data quality improves and policies develop. The HKMA will regularly review the relevant scenarios and refine its assessments to better ascertain the Exchange Fund’s resilience to climate change. As a long-term investor, the HKMA fully understands the risks and opportunities presented by climate change. The HKMA is committed to further expanding sustainable investments and capturing opportunities relating to climate transition, climate risk mitigation and enhancement of long-term portfolio returns. The HKMA maintained its strong momentum in 2022, further increasing its holdings of green, social and sustainability bonds by 50%. In respect of equity investments, the HKMA invests in an actively managed equity portfolio with a governance theme and adopts a decarbonisation strategy for its passive equity portfolio, tilting it towards companies with lower carbon emissions. In addition, the HKMA is exploring with the dedicated general partners of the Exchange Fund’s “Long-Term Growth Portfolio” the establishment of a specialised private equity portfolio to promote green and sustainable development in Asia (Figure 3). Figure 3 Ongoing measures to increase ESG investments The HKMA has invested in a pan-African wind farm operator which, in addition to producing clean energy, places great emphasis on social factors and natural biodiversity. Before the wind farm was established, local villagers used poisoned bait to prevent predators from preying on their livestock, but this inadvertently endangered certain vultures belonging to endangered species. Livestock are important assets for local villagers. To help villagers protect their livestock, the operator built livestock shelters within the wind farm to protect the animals from natural predators. In addition, the operator employs a bird monitoring team to issue warnings when vultures are attracted by animal carcasses occasionally left behind by predators, so that the wind turbines can be shut down to prevent the vultures from being struck by the blades. Reducing livestock predation creates a win-win situation: it protects the villagers’ livelihoods while reducing the number of vultures killed by wind turbine strikes, thereby protecting endangered species. Sound ESG practices can create more business opportunities and open up revenue streams for enterprises, as illustrated by the following supply chain-related operation. The investee company is an integrated logistics and warehousing operator in Mainland China specialising in logistics services for cold-chain pharmaceuticals, chemical products and high-end consumer goods. The company faces continually rising ESG operating standards, mainly because its multinational corporate clients require their service providers to meet ambitious Paris Agreement-aligned decarbonisation targets. In response to these requirements, the company engaged an external consultant to assist in formulating a “Three-Year ESG Plan” to reduce carbon emissions intensity by 50% by 2030 or earlier. This comprehensive decarbonisation plan delivered significant results in 2021 alone. The above ESG measures earned the company the “Low-Carbon and Green Management Case” award from the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing. These achievements and recognition have enabled the company to secure substantial business opportunities, particularly from multinational clients in the consumer and chemical products sectors that place a high value on ESG practices. The growth of ESG investment is closely linked to the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capabilities. In 2022, the HKMA successfully held its 4th annual ESG Workshop, exchanging sound ESG practices with 9 participating private market institutions, including general partners, limited partners and corporates, and promoting sustainable investment opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. In the public markets, the HKMA urged trading counterparties, mainly investment banks, to expand their ESG staffing and research capabilities, particularly in Hong Kong. Mr Howard Lee, Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, delivers the opening remarks at the HKMA ESG Workshop 2022 At the international level, the HKMA actively participates in efforts to develop industry ESG investment standards and practices: As one of the earliest central bank signatories to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA participated in a PRI-coordinated collaborative initiative among signatories to develop standardised responsible investment due diligence questionnaires5, 6 for private equity and venture capital investments, to assist private market investors in conducting ESG assessments of general partners and investment proposals. The HKMA participated in several working groups in support of FCLTGlobal’s research, which aims to explore leading market practices for long-term portfolios and the decarbonisation of private assets, as well as the application of such practices by long-term investors. As a member of the NGFS and a supporter of the TCFD, the HKMA contributed to the NGFS Guide on Climate-related Disclosure for Central Banks, demonstrating its commitment to adopting sound ESG practices. The HKMA also led a workstream under the NGFS “Net Zero for Central Banks” workstream, participating in the formulation of sustainable and responsible investment approaches for the central banking community. The HKMA continues to participate in various industry forums and seminars to share insights on responsible investment and climate change strategies. In addition to encouraging staff to undertake sustainability-related courses and obtain relevant qualifications, the HKMA also gained relevant knowledge and practical experience from the process of engaging external consultants in 2021 to advise on leading industry practices for portfolio climate transition. Separately, the HKMA uses ESG data compiled by reputable external information providers to supplement its ongoing portfolio analysis, thereby helping to strengthen the Exchange Fund’s ESG resilience.

The HKMA is committed to reducing its own organisational carbon footprint, with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier and contributing to Hong Kong’s overall climate goals. While striving to promote environmental sustainability, the HKMA also fulfils its commitments to caring for employees’ physical and mental well-being, promoting financial inclusion and discharging social responsibility. The HKMA is committed to conducting its daily operations in a responsible and sustainable manner. To this end, the HKMA puts sustainability into practice under three pillars: the environment, employees and social responsibility (Diagram 1). The Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee is responsible for leading the formulation and implementation of the HKMA’s sustainability strategy. Chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, the Committee comprises 3 Deputy Chief Executives and representatives from the Risk and Compliance Department and the Corporate Services Department, and submits regular reports to the Governance Sub-Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee. Under the Committee’s leadership, various teams and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing initiatives in their respective areas. In 2022, the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee approved climate targets for corporate operations and reviewed the transition roadmap for achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. During the year, the Committee continued to review progress on the HKMA’s green initiatives, including recommendations for enhancing the HKMA’s sustainable procurement policies, procedures and approaches. Sustainability Governance Structure HKMA Corporate Sustainability Journey In recognition of the HKMA’s commitment to caring for the environment, its employees and the wider community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service awarded the HKMA the “15 Years Plus Caring Organisation” Logo for the 16th consecutive year. The HKMA pays close attention to its own organisational carbon footprint and has formulated internal Green Office Guidelines to manage the environmental impact of its operational processes. The HKMA has incorporated environmental considerations into the interior design, operation, repair and maintenance of its offices. In 2022, BEAM Plus awarded the HKMA a Gold rating for certain renovated office areas. This was the second green building certification received, following the LEED Gold certification in 2021. Awarded BEAM Plus Interiors Version 1.0 Gold Rating The HKMA implemented various energy-saving measures. Total energy consumption6 in 2022 was 4,996.4 MWh (2.8 MWh per capita7), down 24.4% from 2015 (Figure 1). Total Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions8 in 2022 were 2,996.4 metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) (1.7 tCO2e per capita), down 38.2% from 2015 (Figure 2). Figure 1 Figure 2 Greenhouse Gas Emissions Intensity (Scopes 1 and 2) The HKMA encourages paperless internal operations. In addition, the HKMA has implemented a print management system requiring staff to log in to printers to confirm each print request, helping reduce unnecessary printouts and toner use. Where printing is necessary, double-sided and black-and-white printing are encouraged. The HKMA is also preparing to implement an internal electronic records preservation system. Total paper consumption in 2022 was 20.5 metric tonnes (0.0114 metric tonnes per capita), down 65.3% from 2015 (Figure A). Figure A: Paper Consumption Intensity The HKMA’s waste management efforts continue to follow the “4R” principle. In addition to conventional waste, the HKMA also reduces electronic waste by adopting technological solutions such as server virtualisation and private cloud infrastructure. In 2022, the HKMA engaged an external company for the first time to conduct a waste audit analysing the composition of waste generated by its offices. The audit found that food waste accounted for a significant proportion of total waste, prompting the HKMA to launch a food waste recycling programme (see “Enhancing Waste Management” on page 41). The total amount of non-hazardous waste generated in 2022, including general waste and recyclables, was 242.0 metric tonnes (0.135 metric tonnes per capita), down 4.8% from 2015 (Figure 3). The fluctuations in the trend were mainly attributable to work-from-home arrangements during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic and the resumption of office operations after the fifth wave of the pandemic. Figure 3 Non-hazardous Waste Intensity The HKMA gives priority to waste reduction at source and is committed to reducing, reusing and recycling. In 2022, the HKMA engaged a company for the first time to conduct a waste audit to gain a clearer understanding of the composition of waste arising from daily operations (plastics, paper, metals, glass, wood, electronic products, etc.) and to provide waste reduction recommendations. Based on the audit findings, the HKMA launched a food waste recycling programme in November, placing food waste collection bins in all pantries. Food waste collected each day is transported to an organic resources recovery centre in Hong Kong, where it is converted into renewable energy for power generation. Residues produced during the conversion process can also be made into compost for landscaping and agricultural production. In addition, conveniently located recycling bins are available throughout the offices. The HKMA shares recycling tips with staff and places greater emphasis on further improving the sorting of recyclables at source, as well as precautions for handling recyclable items such as cardboard boxes, food containers and beverage bottles. We also continue to organise activities to raise staff’s environmental awareness, explain waste management policies and encourage staff to make good use of office recycling facilities. Food waste collected each day is transported to an organic resources recovery centre Recycling Plastic Items The HKMA operates two data centres, one for operations and one for backup. As they account for a major share of the organisation’s overall energy consumption, the HKMA has adopted green designs and various energy-saving measures, including in-rack air-conditioning systems, light-emitting diode lighting and round-the-clock monitoring of power efficiency. Following completion of a consultancy study on the green performance of these data centres in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations to enhance overall energy efficiency. Preparations have also begun for obtaining green data centre certification. The HKMA recognises the importance of building a sustainability culture and therefore regularly launches various programmes and activities to educate and encourage staff to develop sustainability-friendly habits and adopt green and digital ways of working. The HKMA shares green living tips with staff, as well as annual office-wide energy consumption and paper usage statistics, reminding them to help address environmental issues at the individual level. Staff are also encouraged to make suggestions on sustainability matters. Led by a Senior Manager of the Administration Division, a focus group brings together staff from different departments to brainstorm ideas and concrete measures for promoting a green working environment. Focus group members also serve as ambassadors when new green initiatives are launched. The HKMA encourages the wider community to adopt greener operating practices and has launched a range of initiatives to enhance the operational efficiency of the HKMA, the financial industry and the broader economy while minimising resource consumption. The HKMA’s Submission Through Electronic Transmission system (STET) is a one-stop platform that enables banks to submit documents electronically to the HKMA, covering various regular returns required weekly, monthly, quarterly or annually. Another system, e-Delivery, is a secure electronic communication channel through which the HKMA issues information such as circulars and guidelines to banks. The two systems help save a substantial amount of paper each year. In handling banking complaints and enforcement work, the HKMA has taken measures to support paperless document submission, allowing bank customers to lodge complaints through electronic channels and online forms. The HKMA is also developing a next-generation management information system to facilitate complaint handling and the transition from paper to digital records. To reduce paper consumption, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU)9 has adopted digital signatures in its daily communications with participants, including the issuance of circulars, account opening and account termination letters, and responses to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, the CMU will continue to explore more green initiatives, including the adoption of automated electronic processes for internal and external communications. By promoting the use of the Faster Payment System (FPS) and stored value facilities, the HKMA encourages the public to make greater use of electronic payments in place of cash and physical cheques. More information on FPS and stored value facilities is provided in the “Hong Kong’s International Financial Centre Status” chapter of the HKMA Annual Report 2022. Distributing electronic lai-see is simple and convenient, and reduces the use of physical lai-see envelopes and banknotes, thereby supporting Hong Kong’s sustainable development. To this end, the HKMA continued to actively promote electronic lai-see through various social media and traditional platforms, encouraging the public to distribute electronic lai-see during the Lunar New Year via online or mobile banking services using FPS or other e-wallet services. Major banks and e-wallet operators also organised various activities to attract users to electronic lai-see, such as offering festive user interfaces, enhanced features for greater convenience, and lucky draws or cash rebates. The HKMA Promotes Electronic Lai-see on Social Media For members of the public who choose to distribute physical lai-see during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continues to encourage the use of “good-as-new notes”, namely used but still crisp banknotes, for filling lai-see envelopes. Good-as-new notes reduce the need to print new banknotes, thereby lessening the environmental impact. Feedback from the note-issuing banks indicates that public acceptance of good-as-new notes has been growing in recent years. The Coin Collection Programme reflects the HKMA’s efforts to promote coin recycling. Coins collected under the programme are recirculated to meet public demand, improving the efficiency of coin circulation and reducing the need for coin minting. The programme operates two Coin Carts, which have so far served more than 1 million visits and collected more than 800 million coins with a total face value of approximately HK$1.3 billion. In 2022, approximately 78% of users chose to transfer part or all of the value of their coins to stored value facility accounts. The HKMA has maintained its collaboration with the Hong Kong Council of Social Service by deploying the Coin Carts to collect coins on flag days organised by non-governmental organisations, in support of social services. Coin-counting Machine on a Coin Cart Launched in 2014, the Coin Collection Programme is the world’s first systematic coin collection programme using a mobile vehicle concept. Over the years, it has received numerous local and international awards in recognition of its innovative and environmentally friendly approach to coin handling. The programme operates two Coin Carts, each equipped with two high-speed coin-counting machines to collect coins exchanged by members of the public. Members of the public may choose to exchange their coins for banknotes, transfer the value to stored value facility accounts such as Octopus cards or e-wallets, or donate it to The Community Chest. In addition to collecting coins, the Coin Carts are occasionally deployed for various educational activities, such as student visits.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the climate targets (the “Climate Targets”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the “HKMA”). The Climate Targets were developed with reference to the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual (the “SBTi Corporate Manual”). The purpose of this verification was to verify whether the Climate Targets were developed with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information,” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of information. Our verification work was completely independent and impartial. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: • The Climate Targets were developed with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. Shum Siu-yan Head of Audit Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2023 Verification Statement Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the 2022 environmental data (the “2022 Data”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the “HKMA”). The 2022 Data include total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions intensity, paper consumption intensity, non-hazardous waste generation intensity and recycling rate for 2022, as well as changes in these data compared with 2015 levels. The HKMA’s greenhouse gas emissions data were prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the “GHG Protocol”) jointly published by the World Resources Institute (“WRI”) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (“WBCSD”). The scope of verification covered relevant data for the period from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2022, as well as relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison. The scope of verification covered a total of 6 office and warehouse properties: 4 offices at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 2 warehouses at 5) Luks Industrial Building and 6) Tsuen Wan Industrial Centre, located in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan respectively. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency examined representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 properties. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information,” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checking, and performed reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. Relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of information. Our verification work was completely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the preparation of the 2022 Data. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance regarding the 2022 Data and concludes that: • The 2022 Data are materially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA’s overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shum Siu-yan Head of Audit Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2023

Expanding and accelerating climate action has become the most pressing issue of our time. Almost half of the critical decade for addressing the climate crisis has already passed. We need to reduce global carbon emissions by more than 40% during this decade to have any hope of limiting global warming to within 1.5 degrees Celsius. Yet greenhouse gas emissions continue to reach record highs. The latest climate science indicates that the window for limiting the rise in global temperatures to within 1.5 degrees Celsius will soon close. The impacts of a 1.1-degree Celsius rise in temperatures are already clearly felt by all—extreme weather events such as record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding and storms are occurring frequently around the world, each more intense than the last. Hong Kong is no exception. Last September, immediately after being struck by a powerful super typhoon, we experienced a once-in-a-century rainstorm. Despite our sound infrastructure and ability to respond swiftly to disasters, the impacts were still extremely severe—widespread flooding, transport disruption and damage to roads in many areas. All these are clear reminders that decisive and ambitious climate action is urgently needed. Asia faces particularly significant challenges on the path towards a low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development and sustainability. We need credible transition strategies that appropriately balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means easy. Owing to the region’s rapid economic development and population growth, it accounts for more than half of global carbon emissions. At the same time, the Asia-Pacific region’s high population density and geographical location also make it vulnerable to rising sea levels and extreme weather. As the region’s economies are at different stages of development, while the low-carbon transition will bring new opportunities to some economies, raising the necessary transition finance poses an enormous challenge to others. Market estimates indicate that the Asia-Pacific region will require more than US$3 trillion in low-carbon transition investment annually over the next 30 years. As an international financial centre, Hong Kong has both the capability and the responsibility to harness the power of finance to support the low-carbon transition across Asia. As a banking regulator, market facilitator and responsible investor, the HKMA has devoted significant efforts to the sustainability agenda. The chapters of this report set out the various specific measures and initiatives introduced by the HKMA over the past year. In addition, to strengthen the HKMA’s internal governance structure and more effectively co-ordinate sustainability work across different functional areas, we established the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee last year. For details of the Steering Committee, please refer to the new chapter on “Sustainability Governance”. Hong Kong banks play an important role in supporting Asia’s transition to net zero emissions. In addition to performing our traditional role as banking regulator by ensuring in our day-to-day supervision that banks properly manage climate risks, we also act as a facilitator, supporting the banking sector in financing the low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a green taxonomy framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched a prototype green taxonomy framework for consultation in May and are now refining the framework based on feedback collected during the consultation. In addition, as demand grows for higher-quality and more globally comparable sustainability disclosures, the HKMA is working with other regulators to develop a clear roadmap for Hong Kong to adopt the disclosure standards issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board in June, which provide a comprehensive global baseline for sustainability reporting. The HKMA’s role as a facilitator extends beyond developing frameworks and rules; we are also committed to addressing industry pain points. Many banks are currently constrained by data limitations when conducting physical risk assessments. In view of this, the HKMA will shortly launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform. By simply entering a property address, banks will be able to assess the impact of physical hazards on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios, helping them manage the associated climate risks. As a leading international financial centre and sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong has long served as a bridge, channelling international investment into sustainable development projects in Asia and supporting the region’s low-carbon transition. In recent years, international green and sustainable bonds arranged in Hong Kong have accounted for more than one-third of the Asian market, significantly ahead of other jurisdictions. Of particular note, the Shenzhen Municipal Government and the Hainan Provincial Government issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong in 2023 for the third and second consecutive years respectively, once again affirming Hong Kong’s important role as a green gateway connecting the Mainland with the rest of the world. The vibrant development of Hong Kong’s sustainable bond market is partly attributable to the demonstration effect of the Government Green Bond Programme. Since 2019, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing approximately US$25 billion of green bonds to institutional and retail investors. We have seized every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and broaden the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public- and private-sector green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world’s largest government retail green bond in 2022, we issued the world’s first tokenised government green bond in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the second tokenised green bond issuance; denominated in 4 major currencies and issued in digitally native form, these were the world’s first multi-currency digital green bonds. At the same time, we have proactively introduced various measures to enhance the vibrancy and competitiveness of Hong Kong’s sustainable finance ecosystem. These cover a wide range of areas, including capacity building, data enhancement, green fintech and transition finance. In particular, regarding talent development, in 2023 we launched a new “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners, providing banking practitioners with a structured curriculum to deepen their understanding and professional knowledge of green and sustainable finance. Transition finance is another key area of our work. It provides funding for decarbonisation activities in high-carbon and hard-to-abate sectors, preventing these sectors from being unable to transition due to a lack of financial support. To support the sound development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand Hong Kong’s green taxonomy framework to cover transition activities. We will also broaden the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, which provides subsidies to eligible bond issuers and borrowers, to include transition bonds and loans, thereby encouraging regional companies to raise transition finance in Hong Kong. In addition, we will strengthen engagement with relevant stakeholders and attract private-sector investment into sustainable development projects that have historically faced financing difficulties through public-private partnerships and blended finance. Some of the above initiatives require cross-sectoral collaboration and are primarily co-ordinated by the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional co-operation is equally important. In addition to our longstanding collaboration with the International Finance Corporation on the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks, the HKMA’s Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office also joined the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment and the Green Investment and Finance Partnership as a founding member in 2023. The Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero also announced plans to establish a chapter in Hong Kong. Through these partnerships, we hope to promote capacity building and knowledge sharing, thereby supporting the channelling of capital into sustainable development projects across the region and around the world. To foster new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA also helped organise the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week earlier this year. It attracted more than 1,600 participants from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including leading decision-makers from the global business and financial communities, to discuss solutions for scaling up climate finance in the region and forge new partnerships in this area. Chief Executive Mr Eddie Yue delivers remarks at the Climate Business Forum: Asia-Pacific, the flagship event of Hong Kong Green Week. As manager of Hong Kong’s official reserves and a major global asset owner, the HKMA leads by example as a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been at the forefront of green and sustainable asset investment, progressively expanding the Exchange Fund’s ESG and green asset portfolios in the public and private markets. In pursuit of the Exchange Fund’s target of achieving net zero emissions for its “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier, the HKMA added an actively managed global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition last year, while extending the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another public-market asset portfolio. In addition, the green, social and sustainability bonds prioritised by the HKMA have outperformed their investment benchmarks, demonstrating the proposition of “doing well by doing good”. In the private markets, we continued to pursue green-related investment opportunities and became an anchor investor in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. At the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund’s equity portfolio had declined by 6% and 46% compared with 2021 and 2017 levels respectively, and remained below the broader market level. As a sustainable organisation, the HKMA will continue striving for improvement and formulate our sustainability objectives and plans around the three pillars of environment, people and social responsibility. Specifically, on our low-carbon transition journey, the HKMA continues to strengthen our capacity to address climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures cover emissions reduction, energy efficiency enhancement and waste management, with the ultimate objective of fulfilling our commitment to achieving net zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have developed plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the near term and are making good progress towards our interim target for reducing Scope 2 emissions by 2030. To attract and retain outstanding talent to perform the HKMA’s various important functions, in addition to our green objectives, the HKMA is also committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of our staff. Furthermore, by collaborating with various stakeholders, we contribute to building a caring society by promoting financial inclusion, enhancing the public’s financial literacy and raising public awareness of financial fraud prevention. The climate challenge is immense and exceptionally urgent. As economies around the world move towards a more sustainable future, the process is expected to bring profound changes to financing activities and asset allocation. This transition entails considerable risks, but will also be accompanied by unprecedented opportunities. As a leading global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in addressing these challenges. At the same time, we are well positioned to capitalise on the momentum. The HKMA will fully support the industry in financing the low-carbon transition; continue to lead by example as a responsible investor and sustainable organisation; and work with like-minded partners to advance this critically important global agenda. Chief Executive Eddie Yue

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are global concerns. The HKMA’s objective in its sustainability work is to exercise leadership through its own policies and operations, ensure that Hong Kong’s financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to climate change risks, and support the transition to a more sustainable economy. Through active participation in international and regional organisations, the HKMA will also contribute to the formulation of regional and global green and sustainable finance policies and standards. As the banking regulator, the HKMA will further strengthen the banking sector’s climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. Specifically, key priorities include: conducting a new round of thematic examinations of banks’ climate risk management practices and a new round of consultation meetings as part of a review of banks’ progress in implementing regulatory requirements on climate risk management; continuing work on incorporating climate considerations into the HKMA’s supervisory review process; completing the second round of the industry-wide climate risk stress test, providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and sharing observations and lessons learned with the industry; enhancing sustainability disclosures, including working with relevant local authorities to align the relevant requirements with the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards as the global baseline, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision’s Pillar 3^1 framework for climate-related financial risks; and sharing guidance on best practices for transition planning with the industry. To promote the sound development of banks’ provision of green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to keep abreast of local and international market and regulatory developments and engage with the industry to ensure that banks adopt appropriate sales processes. In addition, the HKMA will act as a facilitator to promote the development of the green finance ecosystem and support banks in financing the economic transition. We will soon publish a local green taxonomy and continue to expand its coverage to encompass more activities, including transition activities. Meanwhile, we will continue to explore the application of technological solutions to help banks identify, measure and monitor their climate risk exposures; one example is the forthcoming cloud-based platform to facilitate banks’ physical risk assessments. To enhance practitioners’ professional capabilities, we will also develop the professional-level module on “Green and Sustainable Finance” under the “Enhanced Competency Framework on Banking” in 2024. Hong Kong is well positioned to serve as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfil this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the proposal in the 2023-24 Budget to expand the scope of the “Government Green Bond Programme” to cover sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bond market; at the same time, the “Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme” will be used to attract more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong. We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions and corporates to raise green funds through Hong Kong, and explore potential synergies between green finance and technology. In addition, we will continue to assist in implementing the Government-funded “Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme” to expand Hong Kong’s green finance talent pool. As Co-Chair of the “Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group” (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies and departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and initiatives promoting the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In 2024, the Steering Group will focus on three areas: sustainability disclosures, the application of technology, and transition finance. As another priority, through the “Alliance for Green Commercial Banks”, the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly launch various dedicated programmes in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis and targeted professional training for banks, and offering practical guidance to assist banks in supporting financial institutions in developing distinctive green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also work to deepen collaboration with the “Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero”, the “Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment”, and the “Green Investment and Finance Partnership”. As a responsible investor, the HKMA has committed the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund’s investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring portfolio resilience throughout the journey towards net zero. Recognising that the objectives of the Paris Agreement can only be achieved through an economy-wide transition, we are refining our net-zero strategy to focus on assets that can deliver positive climate benefits to the real economy, while taking into account the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives. As an environmentally responsible organisation, the HKMA’s decarbonisation strategy will continue to evolve to reflect the latest market, regulatory, technological and other climate-related developments. To further strengthen the HKMA’s climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technological solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. In addition, we will continue to actively encourage staff participation in our sustainability efforts, including launching campaigns to foster sustainable habits and enhancing office processes and practices. The HKMA will also continue to maintain a consistent, efficient and sustainable procurement approach, including assessing suppliers’ ESG practices when selecting suppliers and renewing contracts. Building on the green data centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA is committed to maintaining the prescribed certification standards. For periodic upgrades to data centre facilities, in addition to keeping abreast of the latest technological developments, we will incorporate green design and practices. Meanwhile, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and convergence, and actively modernise internal systems to improve efficiency and minimise potential risks as far as possible. Finally, in respect of our social focus areas, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for colleagues and work with the industry to promote financial inclusion and financial literacy, as well as raise public awareness of precautions against financial fraud.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor and sustainable organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework to lead the formulation of its relevant strategies and policies; oversee the implementation of relevant initiatives; and ensure that sustainability considerations are incorporated into the HKMA’s own operations and working practices. In pursuit of good corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework for its sustainability-related work, with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency. This governance framework ensures that sustainability considerations are effectively integrated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, and provides effective mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability work. The HKMA’s sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which monitor and advise on the HKMA’s work, including its sustainability work; the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which leads the HKMA’s overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; in respect of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and, for other functional areas, relevant groups and working groups, which plan and implement sustainability initiatives relating to banking and market development as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Cross-Agency Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the efforts of financial regulators, government bureaux and departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA’s sustainability work over the past few years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA’s different functional areas1. It provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters in the four functional areas of banking, market development, Exchange Fund investment and internal operations; oversees the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA’s functional departments; assesses the HKMA’s performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and oversees external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. In addition, Executive Directors responsible for key functions relating to green and sustainability matters are invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on the key outcomes of their work and future plans. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA’s banking departments, Corporate Services Department, External Department and Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability initiatives, the HKMA and the SFC jointly initiated the establishment of the Cross-Agency Steering Group2 in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Cross-Agency Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts by the financial sector to address climate and environmental risks, with a view to strengthening Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details of the work of the Cross-Agency Steering Group, see the chapter “Enhancing the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem”.

Climate change is a significant risk facing the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong’s financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong’s climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are exposed to the effects of various sustainability- and climate-related issues in their day-to-day business operations. To continue performing their important functions in the financial system and channel more capital towards green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risks. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks’ capacity to respond to and manage climate risks, and accelerating banks’ efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. The HKMA is committed to developing various policy measures to strengthen the banking system’s capacity to address climate risks. In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to assist banks in maintaining safety and soundness during the economy’s transition to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of the circular, we conducted a survey of selected banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transition planning practices. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices regarding transition planning with the industry, and organise seminars or workshops to facilitate the exchange of experience within the industry. Regarding disclosure requirements, in response to the latest international developments, including the publication of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards in June and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision’s (Basel Committee) consultation on the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks launched in November, the HKMA is stepping up its efforts to refine the sustainability-related disclosure framework for Hong Kong banks. Specifically, the HKMA is working with relevant local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that is aligned with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervision of banks’ climate risk management and provided banks with recommendations to help them further enhance their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process. Climate risk management has now been made a standing agenda item at prudential meetings with bank management. Banking supervisors also use the enhanced CAMEL rating system1, which has incorporated climate risk factors, to assess banks’ risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of implementing the two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process, the HKMA revised the “green” assessment framework to focus on banks’ transition planning practices. The HKMA is also reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks’ capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with a view to encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks for addressing climate risks. Following the end of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with the Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 “Climate Risk Management”, a key work priority under the 2023 two-year plan, the HKMA commenced a round of thematic reviews of climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. The thematic review covered 4 major areas, including governance frameworks for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategies, oversight of climate-related risk management, and organisational culture, awareness and communication. The HKMA made a number of enhancements to the climate risk stress-testing framework, including the introduction of a new 5-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of concurrent economic and climate change shocks. Following these enhancements, and as part of the HKMA’s regular supervisor-led stress-testing programme, the second round of climate risk stress tests was launched in June to comprehensively assess banks’ climate risk exposures and further enhance their capability to manage climate risks. A total of 44 banks participated in this round of risk stress tests, representing an increase of more than 60% compared with the first pilot exercise in 2021. The HKMA also held a climate risk stress-testing forum in November, attended by as many as 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating the sharing of experience among banks, the event helped deepen the industry’s overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review banks’ progress in implementing the HKMA’s Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 “Climate Risk Management”. The HKMA met with bank management to discuss their work on climate risk management and common challenges facing the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks and other publicly available information to assess their progress. The HKMA provided banks with targeted recommendations to encourage and support them in continuing to strengthen their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA’s supervisory expectations. As global attention to climate change and efforts to address it continue to increase, the HKMA has observed growing demand for green and sustainable investment products, and some banks have also offered such products to meet customer demand. In view of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks’ sale of green and sustainable investment products and issued a circular in November setting out the standards that the HKMA expects banks to meet and sharing observed good practices. The circular covers various areas, including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training, and book-building and record-keeping, with the aim of mitigating potential greenwashing risks and strengthening investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of related investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analysis, enhancing banks’ capability to manage climate risks. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot cloud-based platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. In addition, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulators to explore how technological solutions can facilitate physical risk assessment. Separately, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable approaches to combating money laundering (anti-money laundering) through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, thereby reducing the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online common data submission platform to fully automate the financial crime risk data collection process, thereby enhancing banks’ operational workflows for the sustainable submission of anti-money laundering-related data. In September, the HKMA organised the “Green Fintech Competition”, aimed at identifying market-ready solutions to help the banking industry address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability- or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted more than 85 submissions from around 70 companies. In December, the HKMA organised the “Green and Sustainable Banking Conference”, providing a platform for the banking and technology sectors to explore the role of low-carbon technologies and green fintech in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and the Mainland, while also announcing the results of the “Green Fintech Competition”. The event attracted around 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulatory authorities and academia. To enhance transparency across financial markets and improve consistency in green and sustainable finance decision-making, the HKMA developed a local green classification framework with the assistance of a consultancy firm. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the “Prototype of a Green Classification Framework for Hong Kong” to solicit stakeholders’ views on establishing and implementing a green taxonomy. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is fine-tuning the prototype framework and identifying additional areas for the next phase of framework development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force, which has identified environmental crimes as predicate offences to money laundering. Given the interconnections between anti-money laundering and environmental, social and governance (ESG), this area is receiving greater attention from regulators. Recognising the potential risks that climate change may pose to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its existing surveillance work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analyses of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helped further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. As a member of the Financial Stability Board’s working group on transition planning, the HKMA participated in analysing the interactions between the transition plans of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to develop a forward-looking and dynamic perspective for examining climate-related financial risks. On the research front, the HKMA conducted a number of applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial sector and the economy. Research topics included the climate risk exposures of the banking sector and investment funds2, ESG fund flows3, the impact of climate change on property prices4, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance across global supply chains5. The findings of these studies have enhanced the HKMA’s understanding of the implications of climate change and ESG issues for financial stability, helping inform relevant policy formulation. Domestically, these studies help strengthen the HKMA’s ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA also shares its research findings with a broad range of stakeholders through international events on climate-related issues, the HKMA Research Memorandum and various other channels. The HKMA’s “Liquidity Facilities Framework” is a collateralised standby funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. In accordance with NGFS recommendations, the HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, the HKMA helps promote international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, while drawing insights from these discussions to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, supporting international initiatives, and aligning with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to build a richer ecosystem and further advance green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the financial sector’s response to climate and environmental risks, accelerates the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supports the Government’s climate strategies. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key initiatives to support Hong Kong in capitalising on sustainable finance opportunities, with major workstreams covering sustainability disclosures, ecosystem development, transition finance and green fintech. Specifically, a Sustainability Disclosures Working Group has been established to develop a roadmap for Hong Kong’s adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The roadmap will cover 4 key areas, namely sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. A Transition Finance Working Group has also been established to explore ways to support financial institutions and corporates in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group has also strengthened the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sectoral skills training and data enhancement. On data in particular, we continued to promote the use of the climate and environmental risk questionnaire for non-listed companies2 launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to keep abreast of the latest developments in green and sustainable finance and enhance Hong Kong’s position as a regional and global green and sustainable finance hub. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced 3 new key initiatives to capitalise on the financing and investment opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To support skills training for the industry, the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance under the Steering Group implemented the Government’s Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme, which provides subsidies to practitioners, students and graduates undertaking green and sustainable finance-related training and acquiring relevant qualifications. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications had been registered as eligible training programmes or qualifications under the Scheme, and more than 560 subsidy applications had been approved. The HKMA also launched the Foundation Level of a new Green and Sustainable Finance module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners. The module aims to foster talent development in the banking sector and enhance the overall professional competence of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to work with the banking industry to develop the Professional Level of the module to meet the industry’s rapidly growing demand for green and sustainable finance professionals. To help financial institutions and corporates, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises, better understand key climate- and sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and transition planning, during the year the HKMA collaborated with relevant Government bureaux and departments, as well as global partners including CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ)3 and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF)4, to organise a series of seminars and thematic workshops that attracted participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. For students, following the launch of the Sustainable Finance Internship Initiative in 2022, training sessions were held in January and February 2023 to deepen interns’ and university bachelor’s degree graduates’ understanding of sustainable finance. Recognising the potential of technology to bridge climate-related data gaps and improve data quality, the HKMA is committed to making such data more accessible and improving its quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website enhancements to provide financial institutions, corporates and the public with a one-stop source of green and sustainable finance information. Major enhancements included an electronic platform for sustainability disclosures, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, and more centralised, user-friendly and searchable data and resources. During Hong Kong Green Week, the Steering Group also co-hosted the “Catalysing Sustainable Finance with Tech” event with Cyberport and Invest Hong Kong to showcase leading green innovative solutions and Hong Kong’s strengths in green technology. “Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Stream” was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, during which various sustainability-themed events attracted more than 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporates, central banks, international organisations, government agencies, academia and consulting firms. The flagship event of Hong Kong Green Week was the Climate Business Forum: Asia Pacific, co-hosted by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation. The Forum brought together more than 400 guests, including leading global business and finance decision-makers, to discuss solutions for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. The two-day event explored a wide range of topics, including energy transition, decarbonisation of heavy industries, the circular economy, the future development of sustainable finance, and emerging climate technologies in Asia-Pacific’s emerging and developing markets. With support from public- and private-sector organisations, more than 10 roundtables, seminars and other networking events were co-organised, covering topics such as climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, financing the net-zero transition, green taxonomies and financing green development in Belt and Road regions. In addition, the HKMA and the International Monetary Fund co-hosted the Asian Climate Finance Roundtable on 29 February 2024 to discuss key measures for scaling up climate finance and the roles of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. These events formed part of the HKMA’s overall efforts to foster and enrich Hong Kong’s green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as useful platforms for participants to drive new business development, share knowledge and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA launched the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks5 as a collaborative platform bringing together regional financial institutions, banking industry associations, research institutions and innovative technology providers to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held a total of 22 training events and roundtables, attracting more than 7,300 participants from across the world, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas. In October, the Alliance and Crédit Agricole CIB published their second thought leadership paper, entitled “Developing an Ambitious Climate Strategy for Green Banking: A Case Study”. The Alliance and Crédit Agricole CIB jointly published the thought leadership paper “Developing an Ambitious Climate Strategy for Green Banking: A Case Study” in October. During the year, the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the newly established Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment (CASI) and the Green Investment and Finance Partnership (GIFP) initiated by the Belt and Road Initiative International Green Development Coalition. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, and channel more capital towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and beyond. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of a Hong Kong Chapter to support the net-zero efforts of financial institutions in Hong Kong and the Mainland. The HKMA supports GFANZ’s work in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate its commitment to combating climate change, promoting green finance and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. The HKMA assists in issuing green bonds under the Programme. To date, the Government has issued approximately US$25 billion equivalent of green institutional and retail bonds, with proceeds allocated to more than 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Programme, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report detailing the allocation of green bond proceeds and the expected environmental benefits. In the 2023–24 financial year, the Government continued its regular green institutional bond issuances and issued approximately US$6 billion equivalent of green bonds in June. The triple-currency offering covered US dollar-, euro- and renminbi-denominated bonds of various tenors, attracting different types of investors and receiving an enthusiastic response, with orders totalling nearly US$30 billion equivalent. The issuance size of the renminbi bonds increased from RMB10 billion in January to RMB15 billion, with 10-year renminbi bonds introduced for the first time, helping to extend the Government’s renminbi yield curve and further diversify the range of offshore renminbi products. The enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government’s green bond issuances reflected investor recognition of Hong Kong’s commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued the second batch of green retail bonds totalling HK$20 billion, further promoting market development and financial inclusion. The issuance provided the public with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, enabling them both to participate in and benefit from the development of green finance in Hong Kong.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA plays a key role in promoting the development of green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has long been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the HKMA has led investment in green and sustainable assets, requiring its external investment managers to exercise active ownership and integrate environmental, social and governance factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. Investing prudently in accordance with the principle of “capital preservation first, long-term growth”1, the HKMA believes that due consideration of environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and set a “Net Zero by 2050” target2 for its “Investment Portfolio”, the HKMA is committed to continually advancing its responsible investment journey, with an emphasis on sustainability, particularly the pressing issue of climate change, with a view to enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieving better risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA contributes to building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to develop industry practice standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment by the financial industry and the central banking community. Through leadership and collaborative initiatives, the HKMA strives to foster a future in which finance and sustainable development advance in tandem. Figure 1 The Exchange Fund’s responsible investment journey Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is crucial to integrating sustainability and planning a credible climate transition to achieve net-zero targets. To fulfil its commitment to supporting the Glasgow Declaration3 of the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) and the strategic plan of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, the HKMA leads by example by preparing this chapter on the Exchange Fund’s responsible investment in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The overriding guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to pursue responsible investment while taking into account the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks in the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors their implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the Exchange Fund Investment Office’s ESG work. Proposals and work progress discussed at the ESG Committee’s quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office.
