In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets every six months to provide guidance on ESG policies and initiatives across the HKMA’s different functions, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in pursuit of the HKMA’s overall ESG objectives. Figure 2 Responsible investment governance structure of the Exchange Fund Investment Office As shown in Figure 1, the Exchange Fund Investment Office embarked on its responsible investment journey in 2016, initially focusing on managing ESG risks that could affect the Exchange Fund’s financial performance. As sustainability evolved rapidly and moved beyond risk considerations to become a strategic priority for major institutions worldwide, the Exchange Fund Investment Office revisited its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone, when the Exchange Fund Investment Office established a new Business Strategy Division led by the Chief Strategy Officer to coordinate and lead its strategic development, incorporating the responsible investment task force previously under the Risk Management and Compliance Division—now known as the Sustainable Investment Team. This strategic move reflects the HKMA’s shift in responsible investment focus from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainability-related investment matters. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with different teams across the Exchange Fund Investment Office on integrating ESG factors and assists its senior management in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across different types of investments: Public market investments—The Credit, Rules and Compliance Committee, comprising senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into the credit risk model with input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reporting by the Risk Management and Compliance Division. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios (see the section “Promoting active ownership” under “Risk Management” on page 40 for details). Private market investments—The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks4 arising from climate change, as well as related opportunities, can affect the long-term performance and value of the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Emissions Gap Report 20235 published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that, unless further reductions in greenhouse gas emissions are made worldwide, the global average temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The urgent need for more aggressive policies, technological development or behavioural changes to limit temperature increases may intensify transition risks such as asset depreciation or stranded-asset shocks. At the same time, increasingly frequent and severe extreme weather events also pose additional physical risks to investments. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future is aligned with the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG considerations. In 2022, the HKMA set a target for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach, with a clear focus on decarbonisation and transition. The following sections elaborate on this approach. Figure 3 The HKMA’s three-pronged approach to responsible investment In progressing towards its net-zero target, the HKMA favours active engagement over exclusions or divestment from its investible universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund’s primary investment objectives. Outright exclusion of certain sectors or industries would narrow the investible universe, with potential implications for investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition and equipped with superior technologies and sound corporate governance to respond to evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emitting industries. Second, tackling climate change requires the transition of core “brown” industries. Simply excluding or divesting from related investments does not help solve the carbon emissions problem. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries through the deployment of strategic capital and active ownership, driving them to transition towards sustainable and low-carbon practices and thereby bringing about positive change for themselves and the world. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net-zero investment strategy, adopting a holistic approach to pursue transition outcomes aligned with the Exchange Fund’s and global net-zero objectives while adhering to its guiding principles for responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities to facilitate climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund’s portfolio (Figure 4). The HKMA’s responsible investment maintained strong momentum in 2023. In public markets, the HKMA launched a new actively managed global equity portfolio themed around sustainability and climate transition, managed by external investment managers, and extended the use of a customised low-carbon equity index to another externally managed portfolio. In addition, the green, social and sustainability bonds prioritised by the HKMA outperformed the investment benchmark, demonstrating the concept of “doing well by doing good”. In private markets, the HKMA actively builds resilient long-term growth portfolios, capturing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic trends such as climate and energy transition. For example, during the year the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds, demonstrating its commitment to addressing Asia’s climate transition needs. Figure 4 Ongoing initiatives to promote ESG investment The HKMA has invested in a company specialising in producing environmentally friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted household waste, including organic matter such as food waste, and non-recyclable materials. Unlike conventional chemical recycling systems, which rely on energy-intensive high-temperature environments to produce plastics, the company has pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. Made 100% from waste, this plastic material can serve as an alternative to the petroleum-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and consumer durables, offering a sustainable and versatile option. At the same time, the material is compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies such as 3D printing. The company is a staunch supporter of the circular economy. The figure below illustrates the positive environmental outcomes generated by its advanced plastics production process: The MCPP, managed by the International Finance Corporation, is an innovative initiative that combines funding from institutional investors with the International Finance Corporation’s own funds to scale up sustainable financing for private companies in emerging markets. The HKMA committed two tranches of US$1 billion each to the MCPP in 2017 and 2019 respectively, and further collaborated with the International Finance Corporation in 2021 to create a new global climate-related investment platform, “MCPP One Planet”, which is also the world’s first cross-sector emerging-market loan portfolio aligned with the Paris Agreement. Through the MCPP programme, the HKMA has committed to providing loans to 80 sustainable development projects across 19 sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate and manufacturing, in 38 developing countries. The International Finance Corporation collected data relating to MCPP loans. According to its report, the HKMA’s lending commitments support emerging markets and developing countries across areas including economic transformation and human capital development. Specifically, the projects financed by the HKMA are expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 5.6 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent annually, equivalent to the greenhouse gas emissions from an average petrol-powered passenger vehicle travelling 14 billion miles. Figure 5 Projected average annual benefits of the HKMA’s lending commitments to the MCPP since 2020 A green and sustainable finance ecosystem is the cornerstone of global sustainable development in the future. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capabilities.

The HKMA strives to be a sustainable organisation and adopts a multi-pronged approach to reducing its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also places emphasis on employee well-being and social responsibility, and endeavours to promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. As a responsible organisation, the HKMA has set sustainability goals under three pillars: the environment, employees and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee)1, established in October and chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the principal decision-making body for the HKMA’s corporate sustainability initiatives. Formerly the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, it is responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating its vision, strategies and policies on corporate sustainability and social responsibility. At the departmental level, the Executive Director (Corporate Services) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and submits regular progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Focus Group and the Volunteer Services Group support the coordination of corporate sustainability work; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming ways to create a green workplace, while the latter aims to foster a culture of participation in volunteer activities. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transition. The focus is on implementing decarbonisation strategies in its daily operations, including operating green buildings and data centres, practising green travel, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools and greener operating practices, reducing waste, and building a sustainability culture. The HKMA also plans to use carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and adopt carbon offsetting measures for hard-to-abate emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to its daily operations, the HKMA continues to introduce greener operating solutions for the wider community, ranging from channels for banks to submit electronic documents and communicate, to electronic payment and coin collection schemes for the general public. To strengthen and sustain its operational capabilities, the HKMA maintains a professional workforce, builds a talent pool and places emphasis on employee well-being. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages employees to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers engaging social enterprises in procurement; promotes consumer education on financial services; and works with the banking sector to ensure that all segments of society have equitable access to basic banking services. The remainder of this chapter sets out details of the above strategies. Under the HKMA’s overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee2, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the potential risks and threats facing the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as flooding or other damage caused by more extreme weather, may affect the HKMA’s offices and hinder employee travel. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plans to address extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that employees are always prepared to implement business continuity measures. Various measures have also been incorporated into office design to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA’s energy use, air travel and waste disposal. The HKMA has been monitoring its exposure to transition risks by tracking its own greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption and paper consumption. The HKMA’s climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 (air travel) across all areas of its operations by 2050 or earlier. As a near-term emissions reduction target, the HKMA plans to eliminate Scope 1 emissions completely by converting all its existing vehicles to electric vehicles; and, using 2015 as the baseline year, to reduce Scope 2 emissions intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier through various decarbonisation and offsetting strategies. Despite the challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will adopt a multi-pronged approach, wherever practicable, to minimise Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions, such as those arising from paper consumption, waste generation and air travel. The HKMA’s long-term and near-term emissions reduction targets were developed with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology, which was also validated by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The HKMA has appointed the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency to verify the emissions, energy consumption, paper consumption and waste data6 disclosed in this report. The scope and criteria of the verification are set out in the “Statement of Verification” section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the Annual Report 2022, the HKMA published a standalone Sustainability Report 2022 for the first time. The HKMA’s efforts to enhance ESG reporting were recognised with an ESG Award in the Public Sector/Not-for-Profit Organisations category of the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants’ “Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023”. The HKMA was the first financial regulator to receive an award in this category. The judging panel commended the HKMA for attaining good ESG standards, presenting a clear and readable Sustainability Report, and appointing an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report, reflecting its commitment to highly transparent and accountable reporting. In addition, the HKMA received the highest accolade, the Gold Award in the “Non-profit Making and Charitable Organisations” category, at the Hong Kong Management Association’s “2023 Best Annual Reports Awards”. The judging panel commended the HKMA’s annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and making good use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA’s commitment to enhancing financial literacy and promoting financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA’s commitment to caring for the environment, its employees and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the “15 Years Plus Caring Organisation” logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impacts of its operations, and its internal Green Office Guidelines provide employees with guidance on resource use and office waste generation. The HKMA has incorporated environmental considerations into the design, operation, repair and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. When renovating offices, existing furniture and fit-out materials are reused wherever possible to reduce waste, while environmentally friendly construction and decorative materials are given priority. The HKMA has consistently adopted this practice and, as a result, received Gold certification under LEED7 and the BEAM Plus Interiors assessment8 in 2021 and 2022 respectively for parts of its renovated offices at Two International Finance Centre. Improving energy efficiency through the adoption of new technologies and the effective use of existing technologies remains one of the HKMA’s priorities. In addition to promoting good practices, such as switching off unnecessary lighting in work areas outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include using light-emitting diode lighting, motion sensors, setting air-conditioned room temperatures at appropriate levels, and optimising energy use in the information technology network infrastructure. The HKMA’s energy consumption continued to decline, reaching 2.59 MWh9 per person in 2023, down 29.7% from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA’s daily operations, its greenhouse gas emissions mainly arise from the consumption of electricity generated from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO e10 per person, down 45.2% from 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardising equipment, office software and meeting facilities, the HKMA has adopted digital tools and technologies and automated and streamlined workflows to create a digital workplace and enhance online collaboration within the organisation.11 Paperless meetings have become the HKMA’s principal mode of meeting. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, electronic processes are primarily used for various internal administrative matters. The HKMA also encourages employees to embrace green and digital ways of working by replacing paper documents and communications with digital alternatives. Meanwhile, implementation of an electronic recordkeeping system is also under way. The above green and digital measures have yielded positive results. The HKMA’s paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kg per person, a substantial decrease of 64.8% from 2015 (Figure 3). As most international events resumed in-person formats following the COVID-19 pandemic, and in view of the need to promote Hong Kong’s status as an international financial centre, overseas business travel by relevant HKMA employees was unavoidable. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages employees attending overseas events to take direct flights or combine different business trips wherever practicable. At the organisational level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. In addition, the HKMA participated in a Gold Standard12-certified carbon offsetting scheme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; the scheme supports waste-to-energy projects, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue to make similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA’s procurement process takes sustainability and environmental considerations into account. As part of a comprehensive review of the organisation’s procurement policies and procedures, the existing practice of procuring green products has been formalised, with compliance with the environmental specifications in the Government’s “Green Procurement List”, particularly for the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. ESG factors and innovative proposals that help enhance productivity and efficiency have also been incorporated into tender evaluation criteria. Meanwhile, all suppliers are required to undertake to comply with environmental regulations. In line with the “4R” principles, namely Refuse, Reduce, Reuse and Recycle, the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimising waste generation and managing waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to assist in developing targeted waste management strategies. A breakdown of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, is set out in the “Performance Summary” section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA directly participated for the first time in the red packet recycling programme organised by the management company of the International Finance Centre office tower. Employees contributed around 3,000 used but still pristine red packets. These red packets were subsequently passed to an environmental organisation for distribution to the public for use during the following Lunar New Year. As the HKMA’s operational and backup data centres account for a major share of the organisation’s overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centres and achieve optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE)13. In 2023, the HKMA’s two data centres received “Gold” and “Platinum” ratings respectively under the BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres assessment guidelines issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only organisation in Hong Kong to receive these ratings. Enhancing the energy efficiency of the two data centres has long been a priority for the technical team. To this end, the team incorporated green design into renovation works and adopted energy-efficient best practices to lower PUE and achieve the relevant targets, including monitoring the data centres’ environmental facilities around the clock and continuously improving environmental factors such as airflow and temperature settings. As the technical team continued to improve the data centres’ energy use, the HKMA engaged an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review comprehensively assessing the data centres’ green performance and formulating recommendations for further improvements in all areas. The study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after its completion, the HKMA also began preparations to obtain “Green Data Centre” certification under the BEAM Plus certification scheme. The certification process was highly comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the technical team implemented enhancement measures based on the recommendations in the consultant’s report, improving areas ranging from energy performance to health-related aspects of the working environment within the data centres.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority’s (“HKMA”) 2023 environmental data (“2023 Data”). The 2023 Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, greenhouse gas emissions from business air travel, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), their respective intensities, and changes in such data compared with 2015 levels. In addition, the 2023 Data includes the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared with the level when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA’s greenhouse gas emissions data was prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”) jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council of Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, as well as the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison (except for the amount of food waste). The scope of verification covered a total of 5 office and warehouse premises, comprising 4 offices located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and a warehouse at 5) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance as to the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the 5 premises. The verification was performed in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information”, issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion with a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data to its sources, and also reviewed and tested the reliability of the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for collecting and reporting the information. Our verification work was wholly independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the preparation of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 Data and concludes that: the 2023 Data is materially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA’s overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shum Siu Yan Audit Director Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency April 2024

The threat posed by climate change is imminent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed that 2024 was the warmest year on record and the first year in which the global temperature exceeded the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, although global greenhouse gas emissions eased slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached a new high, highlighting the inadequacy of current climate change mitigation measures. As global warming is addressed, climate-related risks will inevitably intensify, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. In addition, current geopolitical tensions, the growing fragmentation of the global economy, the risk of worsening energy security issues, and the uncertain economic outlook are all making it more challenging for countries to address climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Of all regions worldwide, Asia faces the most severe transition challenges. As the World Economic Forum has pointed out, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth, but also the region most vulnerable to climate change. Asia therefore plays a critical role in whether the world can successfully achieve net-zero emissions. As Asia’s leading international financial centre, Hong Kong must strengthen its leadership role and fully harness the power of finance to support and drive the region’s transition. To this end, the HKMA published the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” last year, setting out our vision and roadmap for progressively embedding sustainability into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on strengthening the financial sector’s capacity to address climate change-related risks, while also helping the industry capture the associated new opportunities. At the same time, we lead by example. The HKMA’s sustainability work covers four key areas: supporting the banking sector in moving towards net zero, investing in a sustainable future, financing net zero, and making sustainability more inclusive. The banking system plays a critical role in Hong Kong’s and Asia’s net-zero transition, but banks themselves also face considerable risks during the transition. Under the “Action Agenda”, we have set ambitious targets requiring all banks to strive to achieve net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. At the same time, we require all banks to enhance their disclosures of climate change-related risks and opportunities. While continuing to strengthen banks’ climate risk management, we also provide guidance on transition planning to help them enhance their transition capabilities and better manage the associated risks. We are also undertaking preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong’s sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, with a view to further enhancing the industry’s transparency in related activities. In addition, we are enhancing the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance launched in May last year by incorporating more sustainable activities, including transition activities. By providing clear criteria, we aim to channel more capital into sustainability- and transition-related projects. Climate change poses significant physical and transition risks that could affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund’s investments. At the same time, however, it also presents the Exchange Fund with opportunities for growth and positive impact. Our experience demonstrates that investment returns and positive sustainability impact can be mutually compatible and need not conflict. In view of this, we are committed to striving to achieve net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier, and have pledged under the “Action Agenda” to support Asia’s climate transition through the Exchange Fund’s investments. Sustainable investments currently account for more than 10% of the “Investment Portfolio”. To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the International Finance Corporation in November last year to accelerate Asia’s transition to a low-carbon economy through co-investment. In addition, we published the inaugural “HKMA ESG Expectations” document in September last year to further encourage fund managers to exercise active ownership and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. Financing is particularly important to accelerating the region’s transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for arranging international sustainable bond issuances by Asian issuers, including Mainland provincial and municipal governments, Hong Kong plays an important role in directing capital to accelerate the region’s transition. The “Action Agenda” sets out a vision for developing Hong Kong into the region’s preferred sustainable finance platform, as well as the objective of promoting sustainable finance innovation. From leveraging the demonstrative effect of the “Government Sustainable Bond Programme” to drive green bond innovation, including the issuance of the world’s first multi-currency digital bonds in February last year, to expanding the scope of the “Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme” in May last year to cover transition finance instruments, and launching the “Digital Bond Grant Scheme” in November last year, we have remained committed to encouraging regional issuers to use Hong Kong’s financial platform to raise the funds needed for their decarbonisation transition. A robust transition requires not only capital and innovation, but also the support of an inclusive and accessible sustainability ecosystem. This includes reliable sustainability data, highly transparent information disclosure, and industry professionals equipped with relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, under the “Action Agenda”, we have pledged to support high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures and to help bridge the gaps in sustainable finance talent and knowledge in the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainability disclosures, particularly by providing convenient and user-friendly climate disclosure templates to promote sustainability disclosures by small and medium-sized enterprises. In November last year, we also launched the “Green and Sustainable Finance” Professional Level module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. In addition, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we engaged people from different sectors in sustainability discussions, thereby fostering collaboration and innovation. Within the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations align with our sustainability vision. Under the “Action Agenda”, we have pledged to achieve net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030 or earlier, 20 years ahead of our original commitment. In addition, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainability disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap issued by the Government. We began using electric vehicles in 2024 and incorporated low carbon emissions as a selection criterion in our procurement process. At the same time, we continue to enhance operational efficiency through digitalisation and foster a culture of sustainability within the organisation, inspiring staff to actively participate in sustainability efforts. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and dramatic geopolitical shifts have added uncertainty to global climate action. Nevertheless, climate change is an indisputable fact and is progressively worsening. In addressing climate change, the current circumstances leave no room for complacency. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong’s financial system while creating opportunities for us in the process. As we enter 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, spare no effort in advancing sustainability, and deepen our relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the formidable challenges, we will remain steadfast in supporting the development of a sustainable future for Hong Kong, Asia and beyond.

Climate change is a major challenge facing the present generation. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development in Asia and globally. In October 2024, the HKMA published the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (“Action Agenda”), setting out the HKMA’s vision in this area, including our future direction, the timelines for achieving various targets, and how we expect the industry to work together to advance the relevant initiatives. Through strategic policymaking, strengthened supervisory engagement and enhanced internal operations, the HKMA plans to reinforce the resilience of Hong Kong’s financial sector and the HKMA itself to climate change risks, while promoting Asia’s transition to a more sustainable economy. By actively participating in international and regional discussions, the HKMA also seeks to exert influence and contribute to the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels. As a banking regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the banking sector’s climate resilience and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness during the transition to net zero emissions. Our key priorities for 2025 include: - launching a new round of thematic reviews of banks’ climate risk management practices and conducting a third round of consultation meetings to assess banks’ implementation of the HKMA’s relevant supervisory requirements and further strengthen their climate risk management capabilities; - finalising the incorporation of climate risk stress testing into the HKMA’s supervisor-driven stress testing framework; - continuing to advance the incorporation of climate considerations into the HKMA’s supervisory review process; - commencing preparatory work to formulate relevant supervisory requirements for implementing in the local banking sector the climate-related financial risk Pillar 3 disclosure framework to be issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards); - completing the preparation of a new module GS-2 of the Supervisory Policy Manual to provide banks with guidance on transition planning; and - sharing with the industry good practices in climate risk management and the application of green fintech. In addition to acting as the banking regulator, the HKMA also serves as a facilitator, promoting the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the transition. We published Phase 1 of the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance, providing the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitating the flow of related capital. The HKMA has commenced work on Phase 2 of the taxonomy to broaden its coverage, including by incorporating transition elements, adding green economic activities and including climate change adaptation objectives. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will organise another green fintech event in 2025 to promote banks’ adoption of green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well positioned to support sustainable financing needs in the region. To reinforce this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the Government Sustainable Bond Programme, whose expanded scope will cover sustainable projects such as social projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and set an example for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide subsidies through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme to encourage more borrowers in the region to raise sustainable funds using Hong Kong’s financing platform. We will also step up promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions and corporates from the Mainland and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. Meanwhile, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including by providing subsidies to prospective issuers of digital green bonds through the Digital Bond Grant Scheme. Despite growing market demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures by institutions and corporates, entities vary in their capabilities and readiness to make sustainability disclosures, and some may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their customers with a wider range of climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainability disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how technology can be used to make existing resources more accessible and user-friendly; and collaborate with major local industry bodies to provide the training needed by the industry. The rapidly evolving sustainable finance market requires an expansion of the local talent pool and the closing of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and across the region. The HKMA’s key priorities for 2025 include collaborating with the banking industry to develop professional-level training programmes for the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners, and identifying areas where the industry requires further training through the upcoming Capacity Building for Future Banking 2026-2030 study. In addition, we plan to collaborate with key stakeholders to step up the promotion of the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme and review the scope of the Scheme. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks to launch dedicated initiatives across Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing distinctive market analysis, offering targeted upskilling and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in developing roadmaps for making green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA has committed the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” to achieving net zero emissions by 2050 or earlier in support of the overall economic transition. Through a pragmatic and rigorous approach to responsible investment, we will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund’s investments, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can promote positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to leading by example in corporate sustainability. In line with the accelerated timeline for achieving its net zero commitment announced in the “Action Agenda”, the HKMA will continue to advance corporate sustainability by progressively incorporating environmental and social factors into its strategies, risk assessments and reporting at a pragmatic pace. Specifically, in 2025, we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we focus on material issues. In addition, we will conduct an energy audit and use technological solutions to assess the material impact of climate risks on our offices and operations, thereby enhancing our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Government’s publication of the Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong and are actively preparing to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will remain committed to adhering to the principles of energy efficiency and energy conservation when selecting data centres for planned upgrade projects. We will also expand digital initiatives to promote sustainability and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and enhancing the overall digital experience of our staff, banks and the general public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor and sustainable organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework to lead the formulation of its related strategies and policies; oversee the implementation of related initiatives; and ensure that sustainability considerations are integrated into its own operations and practices. In pursuit of good corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework for its sustainability-related work, with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency. The governance framework ensures that sustainability considerations are effectively incorporated into the HKMA’s strategic planning and decision-making processes, and provides effective mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability work. The HKMA’s sustainability governance framework comprises: - the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which monitor and advise on the HKMA’s work, including its sustainability work; - the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which leads the HKMA’s overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; - in respect of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and - in respect of other functional areas, relevant groups and working groups, which plan and implement related sustainability initiatives covering banking and market development as well as the HKMA’s own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (CASG), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the work of financial regulators, government bureaux and departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA’s sustainability work over the years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA’s different functional areas. - Provide guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters in four functional areas: the banking sector, development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investments and internal operations; - oversee the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA’s functional departments; - assess the HKMA’s performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and - oversee external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as standing members. In addition, Executive Directors responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development matters are invited to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on the key outcomes of their work and future plans. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA’s banking departments, Corporate Services Department, External Department and Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability initiatives, the HKMA and the SFC co-initiated the CASG in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the CASG provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts by the financial sector to address climate and environmental risks, with a view to strengthening Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details of the CASG’s work, see the chapter “Enhancing the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem”.

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the Hong Kong financial system’s capacity to address climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong’s climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are exposed to the impacts of various sustainability- and climate-related matters in their day-to-day business operations and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play an important role in the financial system by directing capital towards green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks’ capacity to address and manage climate risks and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. In October, the HKMA announced the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (the “Action Agenda”), setting out the HKMA’s vision to further consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a sustainable finance hub in the region and support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The Action Agenda comprises eight goals across four areas. To assist the industry in achieving the relevant banking policy goals, we have been undertaking the following work. All banks to strive to achieve net zero in their own operations by 2030 and in their financed emissions by 2050 All banks to enhance transparency on climate-related risks and opportunities In December, the HKMA shared good practices for transition planning with the industry and launched an industry consultation on the draft Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-2 “Transition Planning”. The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks’ capacity to address the net-zero transition and manage the associated risks. In addition, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks’ capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating into the assessment process the relevant factors identified by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) for the effective management of climate-related financial risks, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks, including transition planning, to address climate risks. The HKMA has been committed to aligning local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) and the Basel Committee’s Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainability disclosures and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the Action Agenda. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (Taxonomy) to address industry concerns about greenwashing and help direct capital towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors and is designed to align with the Common Ground Taxonomy and the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while incorporating relevant elements that reflect local circumstances. We have commenced the second phase of work to expand the scope of the Taxonomy and are consulting a broad range of stakeholders to further facilitate green and sustainable financing. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks’ climate risk management and worked to support banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and address climate change. The HKMA also completed all work under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to incorporate climate risks into banking supervisory processes. To help banks strengthen their climate risk management capabilities, the HKMA shared with the banking industry good practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation meetings, mainly including: - establishing a robust governance structure with clearly defined responsibilities for the board and senior management - ensuring effective oversight of key areas relating to climate-related risks: (1) facilitating and overseeing the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a sound climate risk culture within the institution. In August, the HKMA held a balanced supervisory roundtable on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on a range of climate risk-related topics, including the challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning and finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and supported the HKMA’s work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA commenced a round of thematic reviews of banks’ climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 “Climate Risk Management”. The thematic reviews covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA conducted a second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new group of banks in implementing Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 “Climate Risk Management” and understand the challenges they faced. The consultation meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance tailored to banks’ specific circumstances to support their climate risk management efforts. The HKMA completed the second round of the banking sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) in 2024, with the participation of 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups. The results showed that the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks under various scenarios, including one assuming the simultaneous occurrence of climate risks and a macroeconomic downturn. Compared with the CRST pilot exercise, participating banks significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report setting out the CRST results and the good practices observed by the HKMA during the exercise was published in February 2025. The HKMA recognises the numerous data- and methodology-related challenges banks face in climate risk management and has therefore been pursuing various initiatives to promote the use of technology in addressing these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the HKMA launched the Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impacts of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Going forward, the HKMA will enhance the platform in response to user feedback and by incorporating more local data. In addition, the HKMA collaborated with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services industry. During the year, we published a practical application guide and two Regtech Adoption Practice Guides (in English), describing technology solutions for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also held the third “FiNETech”, bringing together more than 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore green fintech collaboration. Recognising that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA incorporates a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing surveillance work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analyses of climate-related risks in various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helped further enrich climate scenarios, supporting central banks and supervisors in understanding the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS published the fifth vintage of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Financial Stability Board’s working group on transition plans, the HKMA participated in analysing the interactions between the transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the “Greentech Adoption Practice Guide for Banks” (in English), providing financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. On the research front, the HKMA conducted a number of applied research projects examining the impact of climate change on the financial sector and the broader economy. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in mitigating monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial sector in the transition towards a low-carbon economy. The findings not only enhanced our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability, but also provided valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem to support policy formulation. Locally, these studies helped strengthen the HKMA’s ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The findings were also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through international forums and various channels, including the HKMA Research Memorandum. The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (HKIMR), the research arm of the Hong Kong Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provided evidence that low-emission firms can benefit significantly from carbon pricing and highlighted its role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The study was featured in the HKIMR’s “Insights from Monetary Research” and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers. The HKMA’s “Liquidity Facilities Framework” is a collateralised standby funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through this participation, we help facilitate international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its implications for financial stability, while drawing insights to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong’s financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA’s “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (“Action Agenda”), the HKMA is committed to strengthening the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to developing Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally, supporting technological innovation in the green segment of the financial markets, enhancing sustainability disclosures across the industry, expanding the local green talent pool, and addressing knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Developing Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform in the region and globally Catalysing sustainable finance innovation Supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures Bridging talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region To demonstrate the Government’s determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds totalling approximately US$28 billion equivalent to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds raised have been allocated to more than 110 government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency and energy conservation. We have seized every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and broaden the features of green bonds, including their currencies, tenors and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public- and private-sector green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the Programme’s impact and further consolidate Hong Kong’s position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the Programme’s scope was expanded to cover sustainable projects and it was renamed the “Government Sustainable Bond Programme” (Sustainable Bond Programme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes a Green Bond Report annually, setting out in detail the allocation of green bond proceeds and the expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing approximately US$3 billion equivalent of institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bond Programme. The three-currency offering comprised Renminbi, US dollar and euro bonds of different tenors. The bonds attracted participation from a diverse range of investors and received an enthusiastic response, with subscriptions exceeding US$15 billion equivalent. Among them, the 20- and 30-year Renminbi green bonds were issued by the Government for the first time and were the longest-tenor Renminbi bonds ever issued by the Government, providing new market benchmarks and further demonstrating the role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enriched the range of offshore Renminbi investment products in Hong Kong. In addition, the strong response from global investors to the Government’s green bond issuances reflected investors’ recognition of Hong Kong’s commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong’s financing platform to raise funds for sustainable development, the HKMA continued to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme launched in May 2021, providing grants for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The Scheme has been well received by the industry. As of end-2024, grants had been approved under the Scheme for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with an aggregate value exceeding US$140 billion. In May 2024, the Scheme was extended for three years to 2027, and its scope was expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The extension and expansion of the Scheme are intended to encourage borrowers in relevant industries across the region to use Hong Kong’s transition finance platform to progressively decarbonise. - Grants approved for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with an aggregate value exceeding US$140 billion (as of end-2024) - Extended for three years to 2027, with the scope expanded to cover transition finance instruments Meanwhile, the HKMA actively promoted Hong Kong’s sustainable financing platform, with encouraging results. In August, the Shenzhen Municipal People’s Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time, totalling RMB7 billion, including RMB2.7 billion of green bonds, RMB1 billion of sustainability bonds and RMB0.9 billion of social bonds. In September, the People’s Government of Guangdong Province issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, totalling RMB5 billion, including RMB1.5 billion of green bonds. In October, the People’s Government of Hainan Province also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, totalling RMB3 billion, including RMB1 billion of blue bonds and RMB1 billion of sustainability bonds. These bond issuances once again highlighted Hong Kong’s unique role in facilitating green and sustainable capital flows between the Mainland and the rest of the world. Through the above measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as Asia’s preferred sustainable financing platform. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, in 2024 Hong Kong remained Asia’s largest hub for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuances, with the total value of relevant bonds arranged in Hong Kong reaching US$43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, namely the world’s first tokenised government green bond and the world’s first multi-currency digital bond, respectively. These issuances demonstrated the Government’s support for regional market participants in applying asset digitalisation and innovative technologies in green and sustainable finance. The HKMA also launched the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November to promote digital bond issuances in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovative development in Hong Kong’s green and sustainable finance market. The working group on sustainability disclosures under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group) has been working towards Hong Kong’s adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards). In December 2024, the Government published the Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong, providing a clear pathway for large publicly accountable entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to support entities at different stages of readiness in achieving high-quality sustainability disclosures, making sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continued to encourage the use of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies (Questionnaire), launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainability disclosures by businesses, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to enable businesses to complete it online (see the QR code below). The HKMA is refining the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly, including by identifying core questions in the Questionnaire and providing common use cases. In addition, we seek to enhance the Questionnaire’s compatibility with other supporting tools on the Steering Group’s website. For more information about the Questionnaire, please visit the relevant webpage The HKMA leads by example by making high-quality sustainability disclosures in its Sustainability Report in accordance with the latest global standards, demonstrating its commitment. The Report contains extensive information, including the HKMA’s climate-related operational risks and its plans and implementation progress towards achieving climate goals. For details of sustainability disclosures concerning our own operations, please refer to the chapter “A Sustainable HKMA”. Given the rapidly evolving sustainable finance market, the HKMA is strengthening skills training for the banking sector and promoting knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders to bridge knowledge and talent gaps. To enhance local banking practitioners’ knowledge and skills in sustainable finance, the HKMA and the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB) launched the foundation level of the Green and Sustainable Finance module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners in July 2023. The module aims to help banking professionals acquire knowledge and develop relevant professional capabilities in green and sustainable finance more effectively, and covers four key work areas: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainability/climate risk management; (3) sustainability disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainability strategy, compliance and governance. In addition, the professional level of the Green and Sustainable Finance module, targeting middle- to senior-level banking practitioners responsible for relevant work, was launched in November. To provide banking practitioners with the necessary training, HKIB, as the administrator of the Green and Sustainable Finance module, launched the foundation-level training programme for the module in May. Following the launch of the professional level in November, the HKMA will work with the banking sector in 2025 to develop the professional-level training programme. To understand the banking sector’s further skills and training needs, the HKMA is working with the banking sector on the Future Banking Talent 2026–2030 study, with the aim of publishing the findings in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the Future Banking Talent 2021–2025 paper published in June 2020. The findings of the follow-up study will provide an important reference for the industry, helping it formulate and adjust talent training strategies and initiatives to support the sustainable development of the banking sector. Through collaboration with the Steering Group, the HKMA also continued to assist in implementing the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme, which subsidises practitioners, graduates and students undertaking sustainable finance-related training. As of December 2024, 85 international and local programmes had been registered as eligible training programmes under the Scheme, and more than 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the 2025–26 Budget that the Scheme would be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international collaboration. As a founding member of the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment (CASI), the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, focusing on global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks and innovative instruments. In addition, the HKMA supported the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) in establishing a presence in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage GFANZ’s network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively takes the lead in developing green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can complement each other, the HKMA adheres to responsible investment principles in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritises sustainable assets, and requires its external investment managers to exercise active ownership. Investing prudently in accordance with the principle of “capital preservation first, long-term growth thereafter”, the HKMA believes that due consideration of environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment work. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieving better risk-adjusted long-term returns. We incorporate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner and continue to explore various investment instruments to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to advancing the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published the “HKMA ESG Expectations” and made the document available to investment partners through its annual ESG workshop and the HKMA website. We collaborate with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to develop industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment by the financial sector and central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we strive to foster a future in which finance and sustainable development advance in tandem. In October, the HKMA announced the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (the “Action Agenda”), articulating its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier and mobilising partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, thereby further reinforcing its commitment to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The overarching guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practise responsible investment while taking into account the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks associated with the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors their implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the Exchange Fund Investment Office’s various ESG initiatives. Proposals discussed and work progress reviewed at the ESG Committee’s quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in pursuit of the HKMA’s overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with different teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office on ESG integration and assists the senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing ESG risks and opportunities, particularly those related to climate, across different types of investments: - Public market investments – The Credit, Rules and Compliance Committee, comprising senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of fixed-income portfolios through regular reporting by the Risk Management and Compliance Division. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios (for details, see “Promoting active ownership” under the “Risk Management” section on page 39). - Private market investments – The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks and related opportunities arising from climate change may affect the long-term financial performance of the Exchange Fund’s investments. The Emissions Gap Report 2024 published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that, unless there is large-scale global mobilisation to rapidly reduce greenhouse gas emissions, average global temperatures will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainty surrounding policy changes, technological developments and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may intensify transition risks, leading to greater market volatility and affecting asset valuations. Meanwhile, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also expose investments to additional risks of physical damage and financial loss. Amid these challenges, the shift by governments and industries towards sustainable solutions also creates investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies and sustainable infrastructure that may offer attractive long-term prospects. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future is aligned with the Exchange Fund’s investment objectives and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related considerations in ESG integration. The HKMA has set a target of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier and continues to advance its work towards this target through an orderly three-pronged approach (see Figure 3). In 2024, the HKMA announced the “Action Agenda”, which reinforced the Exchange Fund’s commitments and efforts relating to climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA favours active engagement over exclusion or divestment from investible assets.
