Investing in a sustainable future Achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio” by 2050 or earlier - Proactively expand the scope and range of sustainable investments, particularly climate-transition-themed investments in public and private markets - Integrate ESG factors into every investment decision, with particular attention to climate change and transition pathway considerations - Establish clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, and require all external investment managers, investee companies and counterparties to follow them - Strive to reduce the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund’s equity portfolios by 67% from the 2017 level by 2030 or earlier Supporting regional transition through investment - Continue engaging with external investment managers to optimise investment opportunities that facilitate transition - Continue identifying and prioritising quality investment opportunities that facilitate Asia’s transition and deliver positive global impact First, maintaining a diversified and robust portfolio is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund’s primary investment objectives. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investible universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can capture opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition and equipped with advanced technologies and sound corporate governance to respond to evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emitting industries. Second, tackling climate change requires the transformation of core “brown” industries. Merely excluding or divesting from related investments does not help resolve the issue of carbon emissions. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries through strategic capital allocation and active ownership, driving their transition towards sustainable and low-carbon practices and thereby bringing about beneficial change for both the industries themselves and the world. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from favouring green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition pathways, with a view to driving economy-wide decarbonisation. As a global asset owner, the HKMA recognises that the long-term resilience of its portfolio depends not only on adjustments within the portfolio itself, but also on broad-based economic transition. While there is no single perfect solution, the HKMA enhanced its responsible investment strategy in 2024 by adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting the Exchange Fund’s and global net-zero objectives. The strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including ESG integration and stewardship in fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilts, and thematic investments targeting various types of assets aligned with pathways towards net-zero emissions. In public markets, this may involve tilting portfolios towards ESG leaders or companies providing climate solutions, complemented by stewardship to drive corporate transition. In private markets, greater emphasis may be placed on investments that facilitate transition. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify investment opportunities that can facilitate climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund’s portfolios. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for more than 10% of the Exchange Fund’s “Investment Portfolio”, with financial performance comparable to the relevant portfolio benchmarks (Figure 5). - Public market investments – The HKMA launched an actively managed global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek green, social and sustainability (GSS) bonds that can provide competitive returns while financing sustainable projects (see the “Enhancing sustainability through GSS bonds” section for related case studies). - Private market investments – The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio and capturing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA also actively identifies and evaluates investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including through strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (see the “Working together to address climate challenges in Asia and globally” section for examples). - Passive portfolios benchmarked against ESG indices - Customised decarbonisation strategies for passive and actively managed quantitative portfolios whose benchmarks are not ESG indices - Actively managed governance-themed portfolios - Actively managed ESG portfolios themed around sustainability and climate transition - Projects with sustainable features, such as renewable energy infrastructure and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed around energy transition and decarbonisation globally, in Asia and in the Global South - Green, social and sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP), managed by the International Finance Corporation and focused on sustainable projects in emerging markets - The “MCPP One Planet” initiative, providing climate-related investments in emerging markets aligned with the Paris Agreement The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a quasi-governmental institution. The proceeds raised from the green bond were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading ageing equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrades included optimising monitoring and control systems and pump performance to generate positive environmental benefits from wastewater management, waste reduction and recycling processes. In addition to continuing to treat wastewater and sludge, these facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertilisers, charcoal, cement and other construction materials, achieving sludge recycling rates of up to 100%. The facilities also use gas generated during sludge treatment to power boilers and generate electricity. The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a multilateral development bank. The bond financed multiple projects, including the rehabilitation of a country’s canal system. As one of the country’s largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess river flows to arid areas. The project’s primary purpose is to rehabilitate the deteriorating canal lining to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water-use efficiency and reclaim waterlogged areas. In addition, the project provides skills training to local stakeholders to promote the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation technologies, such as micro-irrigation, and sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organisation. One of the HKMA’s key priorities in 2024 for delivering on this commitment was its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of the original target and in line with the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda”. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is committed to enhancing staff training and well-being, and strives to promote financial inclusion and improve public financial literacy. Chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (the Steering Committee) is the principal decision-making body for the HKMA’s corporate sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment to addressing climate change, the Steering Committee endorsed in October 2024 a new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions in its corporate operations by 2030, as part of the “Sustainable Finance Action Agenda” (the “Action Agenda”). At the departmental level, the Executive Director (Corporate Services) provides guidance on implementing sustainability initiatives relating to corporate operations, staff well-being and community engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for implementing, communicating and reporting on corporate sustainability initiatives. A Green Office Task Force and a Volunteer Services Task Force, comprising staff from different operational departments, provide an additional layer of support; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming and making recommendations on how to create a green workplace, while the latter aims to foster a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA’s commitment to caring for the environment, its staff and the community at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service awarded the HKMA the “15 Years Plus Caring Organisation” logo for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA’s sustainability strategy continues to be structured around three pillars: the environment, its people and social responsibility. - Focus on decarbonisation and digitalisation in the HKMA’s daily operations, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 - Adopt green procurement requirements in accordance with Government guidelines - Promote greener operating practices across the financial industry and wider community - Build an engaged workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA’s strategic objectives - Foster a collaborative, caring and inclusive work environment that values diversity and strengthens staff’s sense of belonging - Provide a quality work environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle - Foster a culture of caring for the community - Incorporate social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management - Promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy through consumer education activities The HKMA recognises the importance of addressing climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, as part of the “Action Agenda”, the HKMA announced its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of its original commitment. The HKMA has revised its roadmap for the transition to net zero, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its daily operations by reducing carbon emissions, energy consumption and paper use, and recycling waste, while fully leveraging improvements in the power generation fuel mix of local electricity companies. In addition, the HKMA has established a digital workplace to improve efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. The HKMA also recognises the importance of fostering a culture of sustainability and therefore encourages staff to actively adopt sustainable practices through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. Under its overarching 2030 net-zero emissions target, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon insetting tools within its value chain to reduce emissions and pursuing low-carbon procurement wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023 the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions from air travel through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel and participation in carbon offsetting programmes. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and offsetting programmes to cover all other major carbon emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to its physical operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market’s low-carbon transition, from introducing electronic document submission and processing procedures to promoting electronic payments and collecting coins for recirculation. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA’s strategies for environmental leadership, promoting staff well-being and caring for the community. Under the HKMA’s overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing the potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To more effectively assess the potential impact of climate change on its operations, the HKMA identifies different climate-related risks and reviews their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring operational continuity, the HKMA’s offices incorporate a range of measures in their design to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans to incorporate comprehensive measures covering not only its offices but also its communications and computer facilities. The HKMA regularly conducts evacuation drills and exercises to activate backup facilities, ensuring that staff are always prepared to implement contingency measures. The HKMA also continuously monitors its exposure to transition risks by tracking greenhouse gas emissions and waste generated by its operations, as well as energy consumption and paper use. The HKMA’s latest climate target is to achieve net-zero Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions associated with its corporate operations by 2030. These targets were developed with reference to the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative. The HKMA uses the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its corporate emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA’s principal greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions arising from the consumption of electricity generated using fossil fuels. In the absence of individual supplier data, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimating major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods, including capital goods, and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the “Performance Summary” on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and criteria of its verification are set out in the “Verification Statement” appended to the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example by adhering to the same climate-related standards that it expects the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees to follow. As a first step towards green transportation, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this work in 2025 with the aim of achieving fully green transportation. The HKMA continues to incorporate environmental considerations into the design, operation and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in various renovation projects in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and fitting-out materials or traded in old items for new ones to reduce waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and energy-saving measures in its offices and data centres. In its 2024 data centre facility upgrade project, it adopted a modular uninterruptible power supply system to further optimise the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its “BEAM Plus”-certified data centre. The design enables flexible capacity expansion, improves operating efficiency under partial loads, and incorporates advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA strengthens internal virtual collaboration through its digital workplace and streamlines workflows, effectively reducing paper use. In addition, by aligning with manufacturers’ software update cycles, the HKMA extends the service lives of mobile and desktop devices, thereby prolonging the period during which they can be used securely. To reduce office waste, the HKMA follows the “4R” principles, namely refuse, reduce, reuse and recycle, and regularly conducts waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. Recycling bins for different materials are available at convenient locations throughout the HKMA’s offices. To raise the recycling rate, the HKMA added collection bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit netting in 2024. In addition, since November 2022, the HKMA has sent collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA joined the Environmental Protection Department’s “Waste Reduction Pledge for Event Organisers”, committing to taking measures to reduce waste generated by various events. The HKMA continues to prioritise the procurement of goods that meet the environmental specifications of the Government’s “Green Procurement List”, particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their itineraries carefully, for example by combining multiple trips when attending overseas events wherever possible. At the corporate level, since 2023 the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel, reducing its annual carbon emissions from air travel by approximately 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in “Gold Standard”-certified carbon offsetting programmes to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; these programmes focus on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on 22 April 2024 through the end of May, the HKMA held its first “HKMA Green Month” under the theme “Think Green, Live Green, Work Green”. This provided a valuable opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA’s commitment and drive to implement environmental sustainability in its internal operations. The programme included a “Sustainability BINGO Scorecard” encouraging staff to practise green living, a “Save the Planet” quiz, and a workshop on caring for “kokedama”, an indoor plant arrangement originating in Japan; waste audit results were also shared, and an operator of a community recycling centre introduced recycling best practices. To sustain the momentum of “Green Month”, the HKMA launched an approximately 6-month recycling campaign in October, highlighting responsible waste disposal and reminding staff that the cumulative effect of small changes in individual habits can significantly improve the organisation’s overall recycling performance. One highlight of the campaign was the launch of a “Green Actions” video featuring senior executives sharing recycling tips. The campaign also rolled out a series of screen savers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles and electronic reminders, encouraging staff to lead by example in reducing waste and increasing recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to understand their awareness of sustainability and gather their views on proposed green office measures. The survey results will help shape future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong’s central banking institution, the HKMA sees itself as an important agent of change and is therefore committed to taking the lead in accelerating the low-carbon transition and promoting sustainable operating practices across the financial industry and the community as a whole. The HKMA has introduced various measures to improve the efficiency of external processes. Following the successful launch of the “Common Data Submission Platform” in 2023, the HKMA extended the platform’s services in 2024 to cover non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, facilitating their submission of certain regulatory information. The expansion of the platform’s coverage aims to further streamline submission processes for reporting institutions, provide a smoother experience for all users, and reinforce the HKMA’s commitment to sustainability. Other new initiatives launched in 2024 included SurveyTool, which enables banks to respond to HKMA surveys through a streamlined submission process, and a smart information and document management system, which provides users with a centralised platform offering advanced search functions for bank-related documents.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the “Data”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (“HKMA”). The Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), greenhouse gas emissions from air travel, and their respective intensities for 2024. In addition, the Data includes Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting, and their corresponding intensities for 2023 and 2024. HKMA’s greenhouse gas emissions data was prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (“GHG Protocol”), jointly issued by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council of Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, comprising 5 offices located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, and a warehouse at 6) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance as to the accuracy and reliability of the Data and to confirm the adequacy of HKMA’s data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the 6 assets. The verification was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information,” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion in order to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the Data by tracing selected sample data to its sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checking and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanism, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant source data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the information. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. The verification team of Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency was not involved in the Data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the Data and concludes that: - The Data is materially accurate and reliable; - HKMA’s overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shum Siu Yan Audit Principal Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2025
